subdomain: 6.1 Conduct structured discovery and requirement gathering

en.question: A manufacturer wants a Claude assistant to explain which purchasing terms apply to an order. Procurement cites a policy wiki; contract staff cite signed amendments in a separate repository. An amendment can override the wiki, but no one has established repository coverage, access rights, or update delay. A wrong explanation can cause a disputed payment. Which discovery outcome is necessary before committing to a retrieval design?

options.text: An agreed policy of retrieving the most recently edited document, with disagreement between repositories counted as ordinary model uncertainty.
options.note: Edit recency does not establish contractual authority, and model uncertainty does not resolve missing amendments or inaccessible evidence.

options.text: An owner-approved source hierarchy and evidence of amendment coverage, permitted access, update delay, and behavior when authoritative evidence is missing.
options.note: These requirements establish whether the available sources can support the intended explanations within the organization's error tolerance.

options.text: A prompt requiring both repositories to be quoted, with business acceptance based on whether the response presents competing interpretations clearly.
options.note: Presenting both interpretations does not establish which terms govern or address gaps in authoritative source access and coverage.

options.text: A larger retrieval budget and a second model reviewer, with source ownership and update expectations deferred until disputed cases appear.
options.note: More retrieval and review cannot guarantee access to missing authoritative amendments; the unresolved data dependencies belong in discovery.
